# detfield <img src="man/figures/logo.png" align="right" height="138" alt="" />

[![License: GPL (>= 3)](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-GPL%20(%3E%3D%203)-blue.svg)](https://www.gnu.org/licenses/gpl-3.0)

**detfield** turns the detections of a fixed acoustic receiver array into hourly location
surfaces: for each tagged animal and hour, the probability that the animal was in each water
cell. Each surface is a Bayesian posterior over the water cells. Every listening receiver's
count of the tag's transmissions in the hour is binomial in the expected number sent (the hour
over the tag's mean delay, taken as known), with detection probability from your range model
at the distance through water, and by default a receiver-hour spread when the model gives one.
The likelihood is normalised over every water cell, a flat prior over water, and each hour is
estimated on its own, with no movement model
([the model](https://jakebrownscombe.github.io/detfield/articles/positioning.html#the-model)). It takes a range
model you fitted, a depth raster of the water body, the receiver deployments, the detections
and the tag delays, in the column names the positionR packages share.

## Install

```r
# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("jakebrownscombe/detfield")
```

The articles are on the [package website](https://jakebrownscombe.github.io/detfield/). One
of them, [Position fish from a cleaned detection
set](https://jakebrownscombe.github.io/detfield/articles/from-detqc.html), also needs the
[**detqc**](https://jakebrownscombe.github.io/detqc/) R package.

To install all four positionR packages at once, see the
[**positionR**](https://jakebrownscombe.github.io/positionR/) landing page.

## Example

The Stoney Lake example has 70 receivers and a range model. One simulated animal is positioned
here from one hour of its detections.

```{r plot-surface, fig.height = 6.4, fig.alt = "Location surface of stoney-02 for one hour: a compact bright patch among the receivers that heard it, with its 50% and 95% credible regions outlined."}
# Attach detfield and build the Stoney Lake field from the example's curve
library(detfield)
lake <- terra::rast(system.file("extdata", "stoney_depth.tif",
                                package = "detfield"))
curve <- de_logistic(d50 = c(250, 750), d05 = c(500, 1500), depth = c(1, 35))
field <- de_field(water_distances(lake, stoney_track$receivers),
                  de_model(curve, sigma = list(station_hour = 0)))
# Position stoney-02 from its detections between 08:00 and 09:00 UTC
dets <- subset(stoney_track$detections, animal_id == "stoney-02" &
                 format(datetime, "%d %H", tz = "UTC") == "01 08")
counts <- bin_detections(dets, stoney_track$receivers, stoney_track$tags)
surface <- location_surface(counts, field)
plot(surface)
```

*Location surface of `stoney-02` for 08:00 to 09:00 UTC on 1 June 2024, from its
`r nrow(dets)` detections at `r sum(counts$y > 0)` receivers, on 100 m water cells. The surface
keeps the smallest set of cells that holds 99.9% of the hour's probability; the water cells
outside it are not stored.*

The 95% credible region of the hour holds
`r nrow(credible_region(surface, level = 0.95))` water cells, and the most probable cell is
`r round(attr(surface, "bins")$mode_dist_m)` m from the nearest receiver that heard the
animal.

## Articles

- [Fish positioning with detection range
  information](https://jakebrownscombe.github.io/detfield/articles/detfield.html), the Get started page: a
  range test counted and fitted, the field built, and five animals positioned by the hour.
- [Range models: bring your own, or start from two
  distances](https://jakebrownscombe.github.io/detfield/articles/range-model.html) reads a model that varies
  with depth and date into a field for each day.
- [Hourly positions against the true
  track](https://jakebrownscombe.github.io/detfield/articles/positioning.html) scores the hourly positions,
  regions and use map against simulated tracks.
- [Habitat selection: depth use from hourly
  positions](https://jakebrownscombe.github.io/detfield/articles/habitat-selection.html) measures how far the
  depth of position draws falls from the true depth, and what that does to a use-availability
  coefficient, for animals with a known preference.
- [Position fish from a cleaned detection
  set](https://jakebrownscombe.github.io/detfield/articles/from-detqc.html): a detection
  set cleaned by the [**detqc**](https://jakebrownscombe.github.io/detqc/) R package handed
  to **detfield**.

## The suite

**detfield** is one of the four positionR packages, which share one set of column names, one
range model and one lake for their examples, Stoney Lake.

<img src="man/figures/concept_suite.png" width="100%" alt="The four positionR packages: detqc, detfield, arraydesign and its point-and-click application arraydesignR, from your files to the tools you export to." />

- [positionR, the suite](https://jakebrownscombe.github.io/positionR/)
- [**detqc**](https://jakebrownscombe.github.io/detqc/): read, check and filter detections.
- [**detfield**](https://jakebrownscombe.github.io/detfield/): detection fields and positions.
- [**arraydesign**](https://jakebrownscombe.github.io/arraydesign/): design and test the performance of tracking systems.
- [**arraydesignR**](https://jakebrownscombe.github.io/arraydesignR/): **arraydesign** as a point-and-click application.

**detqc** exports the same five figure functions as **detfield**: `theme_positionr()`,
`scale_fill_probability()`, `scale_fill_depth()`, `annotation_scale_bar()` and
`positionr_ring_colours()`. With both packages attached, R reports the later one's copies as
masking the earlier one's. The copies are identical, so either works; attach one, or call them
with `detfield::`. Every map in the suite draws a receiver in the three ring colours:

```{r ring-colours}
positionr_ring_colours()
```
